opening.argument: Consider what the narration actually does. It asks how Bitcoin and blockchain work, then explains Ethereum's broader purpose and the smart contract concept. The crowd sale and its price are presented as historical events, followed by an account of a community vote and a split in the system. Those details place the financial references within a history of Ethereum's development and response to an attack, not a present offer. The closing request is for comments and a subscription, not payment, investment participation, or financial data. Nothing in the cited material promises a return or asks viewers to buy.

citations.quote: After all, how does this decentralized system of Bitcoin and blockchain work?
any developer can make his own program on blockchain and for this, they have given smart contract concept.
Since Ethereum needs further funding to grow, in 22-July-2014, a Crowd Sale was launched. In a 42 day sale, the starting price was $0.31 per Ethereum
Community voted and 85% of the people supported Heart Fork. 30th July 2016, Heart Fork is implemented after Whitelick approval. And System has become divided in 2 parts.
